question: Which welding process uses a non-consumable tungsten electrode and an inert shielding gas to produce high-quality welds on non-ferrous metals?
options: Gas Metal Arc Welding (GMAW)
Shielded Metal Arc Welding (SMAW)
Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (GTAW)
Flux-Cored Arc Welding (FCAW)

question: When performing a Charpy impact test on a welded joint, what property of the weld metal is primarily being evaluated?
options: Tensile strength
Hardness
Toughness and notch impact resistance
Ductility under static load

question: In structural steel fabrication, which welding symbol annotation indicates a weld that must be performed on the site after delivery, rather than in the fabrication shop?
options: Weld-all-around symbol
Field weld flag symbol
Melt-through symbol
Contour finish symbol

question: A welder is joining 316L stainless steel pipe for a chemical processing plant. Which filler metal classification would be most appropriate to maintain corrosion resistance and low carbon content?
options: ER70S-6
ER308L
ER316L

question: What is the primary purpose of preheating high-carbon steel before welding?
options: To increase the deposition rate of the filler metal
To reduce the risk of hydrogen-induced cold cracking by slowing the cooling rate
To eliminate porosity caused by surface contamination
To increase penetration depth of the weld pool

question: In plasma arc cutting, what distinguishes the transferred arc mode from the non-transferred arc mode?
options: In transferred arc mode, the arc is established between the electrode and the nozzle only
In transferred arc mode, the arc extends from the electrode through the orifice to the workpiece
In non-transferred arc mode, the workpiece forms part of the electrical circuit
In transferred arc mode, no plasma gas is required

question: When calculating the heat input for a GTAW process, which formula is correct?
options: Heat Input (kJ/mm) = (Amps × Volts) / (1000 × Travel Speed mm/min)
Heat Input (kJ/mm) = (Amps × Volts × 60) / (1000 × Travel Speed mm/min)
Heat Input (kJ/mm) = (Volts × Travel Speed) / (Amps × 1000)
Heat Input (kJ/mm) = (Amps + Volts) × Travel Speed / 1000

question: Which destructive test method is used to evaluate the bend ductility and soundness of a welded joint by wrapping it around a former of specified radius?
options: Macro examination test
Guided bend test
Nick break test
Fillet weld fracture test

question: In SMAW, an electrode classified as E7018 is characterized by which of the following properties?
options: Cellulosic coating, AC only, 70 ksi tensile strength, used for vertical-down welding
Low-hydrogen iron powder coating, all positions except vertical-down, 70 ksi tensile strength
Rutile coating, DC positive only, 80 ksi tensile strength, flat position only
Oxidizing coating, AC/DC negative, 70 ksi tensile strength, used for cast iron

question: What type of weld discontinuity is described as a crack that runs parallel to the weld axis in the heat-affected zone, typically caused by hydrogen embrittlement and residual stress?
options: Hot crack
Longitudinal HAZ cold crack (underbead crack)
Crater crack
Lamellar tear

question: During the fabrication of a pressure vessel in accordance with ASME Section VIII, what is the significance of the minimum design metal temperature (MDMT)?
options: It defines the maximum allowable working pressure of the vessel
It specifies the lowest temperature at which the vessel material can be used without risk of brittle fracture
It determines the required post-weld heat treatment temperature range
It establishes the hydrostatic test pressure for the vessel

question: Which non-destructive testing method is MOST effective for detecting surface and near-surface cracks in austenitic stainless steel weldments?
options: Magnetic particle testing (MT)
Radiographic testing (RT)
Liquid penetrant testing (PT)
Ultrasonic testing (UT) using shear wave

question: In GMAW short-circuit transfer mode, which combination of parameters is most characteristic?
options: High voltage (32-40V), high wire feed speed, large droplet transfer
Low voltage (14-22V), low to moderate wire feed speed, low heat input
Medium voltage (24-28V), spray droplets, used for thick materials only
High voltage (28-36V), pulsed current, used for thin sheet metal

question: What is lamellar tearing in welded fabrications, and which material characteristic makes steel susceptible to it?
options: A hot crack in the weld pool caused by high sulfur content in the filler wire
A subsurface cracking in the base metal below the HAZ caused by through-thickness tensile stress in steel with poor short transverse ductility due to non-metallic inclusions
A type of porosity caused by hydrogen absorption during welding of high-strength steel
A surface crack caused by excessive interpass temperature in multi-pass welds

question: When developing a Welding Procedure Specification (WPS) in accordance with AWS D1.1, which of the following represents an essential variable that, if changed, requires requalification of the procedure?
options: A minor change in the root face dimension within the specified tolerance
A change in base metal P-Number grouping
A change in the brand name of a pre-qualified shielding gas mixture within the same composition
A reduction in the number of weld passes that does not affect the groove geometry
